thread:
maya: quick q — when we hedge and fallback midflight to a cheaper model, how do people feel about carrying the original request context (user locale, tenant flags, prompt metadata) vs. truncating to a minimal header set? concern is both correctness and not leaking extra tenant metadata to fallback variants.
andre: i'd prefer keeping request-id, tenant-id (hashed), locale, and an explicit fallback-reason tag. minimal but useful.
sachin: +1 on hashed tenant-id. also we should tag model-chain so logs show modelA->modelB. otherwise debugging is a nightmare.
linda: question: do we treat fallback as a new request for billing/quotas? that affects how downstreams count tokens/calls.
maya: good call. my inclination: billing counts should be attributed to the original request owner and split by model actually used for tokens. fallback should surface which model generated which token chunks.
nate: technically doable if we emit per-chunk provenance in the stream trailers. streaming clients can ignore if they don't care.
andre: example proto for trailers: 
```
trailers: {
  x-rw-id: "req-123",
  x-rw-model-chain: "redwood-xl->redwood-compact",
  x-rw-fallback-reason: "timeout-hedge",
  x-rw-provenance: "chunks:0-120:modelA;121-512:modelB"
}
```
sachin: that provenance string might get big. maybe encode as a small JSON blob or compressed base64 in header? but headers/trailers have size limits.
linda: can we just record chunk boundaries in observability instead of sending to clients? i worry about client-side parsing and ecosystems not supporting complex trailers.
nate: agreed — default: minimal headers for clients, detailed per-chunk provenance to observability backend and to our console. allow opt-in expanded trailers for advanced clients via a request flag `x-rw-debug-provenance`.
maya: ok tradeoffs: 1) privacy/isolation — hashed tenant-id only 2) debuggability — model-chain + observability provenance 3) client surface — minimal by default, opt-in detailed trailers. sound reasonable?
andre: yes. also need to ensure fallback doesn't break idempotency semantics. if original request had side-effects, we must avoid double-exec on fallback 
edge-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure `x-rw-request-id` is immutable across hedges, add config flag `edge.fallback.propagate_context` default false, add observability tag `rw.fallback=true`
sachin: implementation note — for streaming we need to stitch KV-cache context if we switch models midflight. smaller model might not accept full tokenized context. we should send a checkpoint token window and a trimmed context blob.
maya: yep — propose middleware flow: 
1) Accept request with full context.
2) If hedge triggers, evaluate compatibility score against fallback model.
3) If compatible, forward full context; else compute trim window and annotate `x-rw-trimmed=true` with trimmed-range.
andre: can we reuse existing prefix cache keys with a `model-compat` namespace so caches don't collide? e.g. `cache:tenant:prefix:model-a:v1` vs `cache:tenant:prefix:model-b:v1`
linda: that will increase cache size but prevents serving wrong completions. probably acceptable per-tenant.
nate: one more thing — backpressure: if fallback starts producing slower than primary, hedging policy must stop spawning more fallbacks midflight. otherwise we blow up concurrency. add a per-request hedge-budget header.
maya: great points. i'll draft a short RFC pull with the middleware flow and opt-in header flags. tagging @andre @sachin for review. :thumbsup:
